ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Duke Kahanamoku Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Establishing care for six weeks of breathlessness, ankle swelling and tiredness five years after a heart attack: examination, ECG, chest X-ray, NT-proBNP and laboratory tests, a diuretic, and the plan for an echocardiogram. Concerns: He wants to get back in the ocean, to swim and surf again; He wants to keep working as sheriff; He wants his ʻohana involved as he chooses and his own ways of healing respected. [S]

tr.td: Twelve-lead electrocardiogram: sinus rhythm at 92 per minute, Q waves in V1 to V4 from an old anterior infarction, QRS 104 ms, no left bundle branch block, no atrial fibrillation
Chest X-ray, two views: enlarged heart, upper-lobe venous diversion and small pleural effusions on both sides; no pneumonia

Transthoracic echocardiography: ejection fraction 30% by biplane method, thinned and akinetic anterior wall and apex, no left ventricular thrombus, dilated left ventricle (end-diastolic diameter 62 mm), moderate functional mitral regurgitation, normal right ventricle, estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 42 mmHg

Invasive coronary angiography by the radial route: chronic total occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending artery filling faintly by collaterals from the right coronary artery, 40% narrowing of the mid right coronary artery and 30% of the circumflex; no lesion suitable for or likely to benefit from revascularization, given the thinned, scarred anterior wall
Twelve-lead electrocardiogram at the sick visit: sinus rhythm at 96 per minute, old anterior Q waves unchanged, no peaked T waves, no change in QRS width
Outpatient cardiac rehabilitation for heart failure: 36 sessions over twelve weeks, with supervised pool swimming in the last month and an ocean-safety plan; all sessions completed
Advance care planning conversation, about 25 minutes, with his consent

Transthoracic echocardiography after more than 90 days of therapy: ejection fraction 38% by biplane method, anterior wall and apex still thinned and akinetic, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter 58 mm (from 62), mild mitral regurgitation (from moderate), no thrombus, estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure 30 mmHg
Respiratory syncytial virus vaccine, single dose

list.item: Sheriff of Honolulu, elected many times; a former Olympic champion swimmer and a surfer who helped carry surfing to the world; until six weeks ago he swam and surfed at Waikīkī most mornings [S]
Native Hawaiian, born and raised in Honolulu; asked to be called Mr. Kahanamoku in the clinic; speaks English with Hawaiian words where he prefers them [S]
ʻOhana: he wants members of his ʻohana present for big decisions when he chooses, and he makes the decisions; lives at home in Honolulu [S]
Tobacco: never. Alcohol: never. No drug use [S]
Diet: fish, poi, rice, fruit and greens at home; salted and dried fish and shoyu at times; many meals at public events where food is salty [S]
Income: a county salary as sheriff; modest means; county health plan with Medicare [S]

Traditional healing: he has his own Native Hawaiian practices and will decide whether and how they are part of his care; lomilomi through a Native Hawaiian Health Care System was offered alongside clinic care, and nothing further was asked [S]
Strengths: a lifetime of discipline in training, calm under pressure, deep knowledge of the ocean, and a wide circle in the community [S]

tr.td: Establishing care for six weeks of breathlessness, ankle swelling and tiredness five years after a heart attack: examination, ECG, chest X-ray, NT-proBNP and laboratory tests, a diuretic, and the plan for an echocardiogram
Two-week review: echocardiogram, heart failure cardiology consultation the same day, the diagnosis, and guideline-directed medicines
Two-week review after sacubitril-valsartan, carvedilol and empagliflozin: kidney function, potassium, angiography result and the next medicine
Two-week review, five days after the sick visit: kidney function and potassium, medicine doses, lipids, and cardiac rehabilitation adapted to the ocean
Six-month review: repeat echocardiogram after more than 90 days of therapy, the defibrillator decision, iron, the delayed titration step, and plans for the year
Same-day sick visit for vomiting and diarrhea on heart failure medicines
Culturally safe care: address him as Mr. Kahanamoku, as he asked; take time; explain each test and medicine plainly; involve his ʻohana as he chooses while he makes the decisions

Heart failure cardiology consultation on the day of the two-week visit, with an echocardiogram, to confirm the diagnosis and its cause and to plan guideline-directed medical therapy, ischemic evaluation and device decisions
Furosemide 40 mg every morning for congestion, with a daily weight and a written plan; metabolic panel and magnesium in one to two weeks; lower the dose when he is dry
Baseline tests: ECG, chest X-ray, NT-proBNP, metabolic panel and magnesium, blood count, iron studies, TSH, hemoglobin A1c, lipids and ALT; echocardiogram at the two-week visit
Atorvastatin raised from 40 to 80 mg for LDL 92 mg/dL; lipid panel in four to twelve weeks; goal below 70 mg/dL
Sodium: less salted and dried fish, shoyu and salty party food, using the foods he already eats; no routine fluid restriction; daily weights
Vaccinations: pneumococcal, influenza, COVID-19 and RSV as due, because heart disease raises the risk of severe respiratory infection

Native Hawaiian healing alongside clinic care, if he wishes: lomilomi through Ke Ola Mamo, a Native Hawaiian Health Care System; he will tell the clinic before using any plant medicine so that interactions can be checked; the clinic asks nothing further about his practices

Guideline-directed medical therapy: stop lisinopril and start sacubitril-valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily 36 hours after the last dose; change metoprolol tartrate to carvedilol 3.125 mg twice daily; empagliflozin 10 mg daily; add spironolactone when potassium and kidney function allow; raise one medicine every two weeks toward target doses, with a metabolic panel one to two weeks after each change
Intravenous ferric carboxymaltose 750 mg at the two-week visit and again two weeks later, for iron deficiency in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; iron studies again at about six months
Invasive coronary angiography within two weeks to define the coronary disease and whether revascularization could help
Defibrillator decision: repeat echocardiogram after at least 90 days of optimized therapy; a primary-prevention ICD if the ejection fraction stays at 35% or below with NYHA class II to III

Sick-day rules: on days of vomiting, diarrhea or not drinking, hold empagliflozin, furosemide, spironolactone and sacubitril-valsartan, keep carvedilol if blood pressure allows, drink small amounts often, and restart when eating and drinking normally for a day; a written card

Cardiac rehabilitation for heart failure, 36 sessions, adapted to an ocean athlete: pool swimming in the program, then calm water inside the reef with a companion and near a lifeguard, no breath-hold diving, no big surf until cleared, water through the morning, and out of the water at once for chest pain, lightheadedness or unusual breathlessness
Laboratory tests drawn at the clinic on the day of each medicine change or by the clinic's nurse at home, with nurse calls to titrate doses between visits
Euvolemia: no ankle swelling or orthopnea, with a steady dry weight
Dry weight about 93 kg; no edema or orthopnea; furosemide reduced to 20 mg
All four guideline-directed medicines at the highest doses he tolerates within three months

All four classes started within two weeks of diagnosis; carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, empagliflozin and spironolactone at their doses; sacubitril-valsartan stayed at the starting dose for five months after a missed titration step and was raised at six months
KCCQ-12 at least 20 points higher and NYHA class I to II within six months
KCCQ-12 38 to 80; NYHA class I to II
Back in the ocean safely, swimming in calm water with a companion
Swimming three mornings a week in calm water inside the reef with a friend, after cardiac rehabilitation

list.item: Independent in all daily activities; breathless walking up a gentle slope or paddling out through small surf; has stopped his morning swim after a few minutes; sleeps on two pillows; NYHA class III [S]
Alert, calm and courteous; frustrated at being kept from the water; mood steady; PHQ-2 score 1 [S]
